source_review.notes: Reviewed the original Count-Min publication record and encyclopedia treatment, the primary conservative-update traffic paper, empirical-error estimator paper, Count Sketch paper, primary frequent-items evaluation, and current Apache DataSketches API. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200 or 202. Theorem, estimator, implementation, and empirical claims remain scoped to their cited models.

evidence: Checked universe U, vector coordinate f_x, l1 mass, width w, depth d, row hashes h_j, counters C[j,k], collision noise Z_j, estimate, epsilon, and delta.
Checked insertion-only, strict-turnstile, and general-turnstile models remain distinct.
Checked pointwise, predetermined simultaneous, and adaptive-query probability scopes are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Additive error is consistently expressed against total l1 mass rather than the queried coordinate.

evidence: Recomputed compact sizing as ceil(e/0.01)=272, ceil(ln 10^6)=14, and 272*14=3808 counters.
Recomputed example sizing as width 1360, depth 12, 16320 counters, and 130560 raw bytes.
Recomputed one-row expectation 2000000/272=7352.941176 and Markov ratio 0.3676470588, below 1/e.
Recomputed simultaneous-query depth 19; exercise width 544, depth 17, 9248 counters, 36992 bytes; and fraud epsilon 2.5e-5.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All byte counts exclude object headers, allocator effects, alignment, seeds, and envelope metadata as stated.

evidence: Derived each selected counter as f_x plus nonnegative collision noise Z_j in the insertion-only model.
Derived E[Z_j] <= ||f||_1/w from pair collision probability and linearity of expectation.
Applied Markov at w=ceil(e/epsilon) and independent row repetition at d=ceil(ln(1/delta)).
Verified cellwise linear merge from fixed hash indicators and showed why state-dependent conservative update is not the same linear map.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Negative updates and adaptive adversarial queries are explicitly excluded from the simple one-sided proof.

evidence: Reviewed empty and high-mass streams, rare and heavy keys, absent-key estimates, weighted updates, negative corrections, and same-collider rows.
Reviewed wrap, saturation, checked overflow, partial row writes, concurrent mixed snapshots, crashes, reset races, and late events.
Reviewed incompatible seeds, encodings, modes, dimensions, namespaces, duplicated or overlapping epochs, malformed envelopes, and chosen collisions.
Reviewed candidate eviction, unbounded/adaptive queries, conservative shard merges, and reconstruction after overflow.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture excludes signed updates, overflow, concurrency, persistence, malformed serialization, randomized trials, adversarial keys, and candidate-system behavior.

evidence: The standard fixture sends total mass 27 to every one of three rows and checks every row sum equals 27.
Every inserted key's standard estimate is checked to be at least its exact frequency.
Cellwise addition of two disjoint standard shard matrices exactly equals the full-stream matrix.
The fixture reproduces total inserted-key overestimate 26 for standard update and 9 for conservative update, with key 45 estimated as 13 and 7 versus truth 2.
invariant_checking.notes: The modular hash family is intentionally transparent teaching machinery, not production hashing evidence.

evidence: Reviewed the point-query theorem line by line through nonnegative noise, pairwise collision probability, expectation, Markov, independent depth, and minimum estimator.
Reviewed merge identity cell by cell and tied fixed indicators to the serialized compatibility fields.
Reviewed no-underestimate as a deterministic insertion-only invariant separate from the probabilistic additive upper bound.
Reviewed the candidate-gate logic: below-threshold estimates exclude, above-threshold estimates require exact confirmation for costly actions.
proof_review.notes: No universal simultaneous/adaptive-query theorem, signed-stream theorem, or production concurrency/durability proof is claimed.

evidence: The formal point and merge arguments state premises and conclusions separately from intuition and engineering policy.
Conservative-update fixture improvement is labeled empirical and finite rather than a universal dominance result.
Range, inner-product, heavy-hitter, and current-library statements are not presented as automatic consequences of the basic point-query theorem.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter distinguishes mathematical model, estimator guarantee, implementation invariant, deployment protocol, and decision policy.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent arithmetic reproduced every published sizing, expectation, probability-ratio, byte, and threshold value in the chapter.
All seven external destinations resolved and repository-local front-matter, Markdown, local-link, section, example, exercise, answer, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production hash, randomized failure-rate experiment, large trace, throughput benchmark, overflow test, concurrent snapshot, crash recovery, distributed replay, candidate table, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives the additive point guarantee, marks its insertion-only and fixed-query boundary, separates estimation from enumeration, and treats merge identity as a full representation contract.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed key encoding, seeds, counter arithmetic, atomic visibility, persistence, envelope versioning, compatible merge, lineage deduplication, reset, candidate confirmation, adversarial hashing, metrics, testing, and rollback/rebuild.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet exposes the theorem and pitfalls; the executable model contrasts standard and conservative updates; ten examples cover derivation, rare keys, merge, retries, signed updates, overflow, candidate gating, and query budgeting; five exercises progress to distributed and fraud-system transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/publisher/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Cormode, Muthukrishnan, Estan, Varghese, Ting, Charikar, Chen, Farach-Colton, Hadjieleftheriou, Apache, streaming-systems, database, distributed-systems, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production Count-Min or Count Sketch implementation, concrete deployed failure rate, adaptive-query protection, concurrent/persistent merge protocol, certification, nor deployment fitness.
